question: Does exact query-span projection inside merged OCR lines preserve multiscale recall gain while eliminating wrong-carrier regression on the next unconsumed HierText test cohort, with zero accepts for queries proven absent by exhaustive truth?

source_contract.selection_authority: official exhaustive legible printed word transcripts and polygons only
source_contract.negative_authority: first subsequent selected target under cyclic order that is not contained in any complete current-image truth token

selection_contract.per_image_target: largest normalized-area eligible unique word; lexical tie broken by normalized token
selection_contract.absent_query: first subsequent target in cyclic cohort order that is not contained in any complete normalized legible printed word truth in the current image

algorithm_contract.baseline: single full-resolution frame, exact normalized target token, candidate confidence at least 0.45
algorithm_contract.successor: baseline observations plus four deterministic 60%-width by 60%-height corner fields enlarged 1.5x; rank exact token first, then a unique exact query substring occupying at least 25% of the OCR token with its quadrilateral projected to the character span, then edit-distance one token when both strings have at least six characters
algorithm_contract.query_span_projection: linearly interpolate both long edges of the OCR quadrilateral by normalized target start/end character offsets
algorithm_contract.candidate_binding: projected or native accepted OCR box must cover at least half of the selected target truth bbox; otherwise WRONG_CARRIER
algorithm_contract.negative_acceptance: any accepted candidate for a truth-absent and substring-disjoint query is a false accept

claim_boundary: A fresh, disjoint 30-image cohort from previously unused HierText test pixels plus official exhaustive word truth supports a static goal-conditioned OCR carrier Development result only. Query-span projection is an OCR-box geometry mechanism; it does not establish an exact real-world referent, facade, sign, portal, entrance ownership, public access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, user benefit, deployment, or safety. UNKNOWN is neither negative nor known-safe. This cohort is consumed after the run; no conformal, FDR, or open-world guarantee is claimed.
